v.why: Very small learning rates are under-trained in 243 epochs, so increasing them helps (e.g. experiments 1 and 2).
Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence, as in experiments 8 and 9.
Stepping down from an unstable learning rate recovers accuracy (experiments 14, 15, 20).
Lowering an already small learning rate leaves the network under-trained.
Strong L2 penalty underfits, so weakening it helps (experiments 89, 90, 98).
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty worsens underfitting.
Deeper nets are more unstable at high learning rates, so removing a layer helps (experiments 78, 75).
At low learning rates a deeper net adds capacity and effective update size, which helps (experiments 61, 65).
Wider nets train faster per step at low learning rates (experiment 44).
Larger batches mean fewer updates, which hurts when the learning rate is already too small to converge in 243 epochs.

With only 243 epochs, a very low learning rate is under-trained, and a very high one diverges. The alpha pattern is less certain, resting on a few large gains from stepping down at high alpha.
